subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Assembly Line: Ford's Moving Revolution
description: Learn The Assembly Line: Ford's Moving Revolution in one minute.

hook.text: Before Ford, one worker built one car. It took 12 hours per vehicle.

buildup.text: Ford moved the car past workers on a chain. Each person did one task.

discovery.text: Assembly time dropped from 12 hours to 93 minutes. Costs plummeted.

twist.text: Ford paid workers $5 a day — double the norm — so they could buy the cars.

climax.text: The moving assembly line turned the car from a luxury into an everyday tool.

punchline.text: Move the work to the worker and the world speeds up.

quiz.question: How did Ford's assembly line cut costs so dramatically?
options: He used cheaper materials than other car makers
Each worker did one repeated task as the car moved past, cutting assembly time
He automated the entire process with robots
